title: EXPLAIN & EXPLAIN ANALYZE
description: Read PostgreSQL query execution plans, interpret Sequential Scan, Index Scan, Bitmap Heap Scan, and detect plan cost estimation errors.

data.text: **`EXPLAIN`** shows the query plan generated by the PostgreSQL cost-based optimizer without executing the query. **`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`** actually runs the query, displaying both estimated costs and real-world execution metrics (actual execution time, buffer cache hits, and rows returned).

data.title: Comprehensive EXPLAIN ANALYZE Command
data.content: Captures buffer cache hits and actual timing.
data.code:
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, VERBOSE, SETTINGS)
SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) 
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.created_at >= '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY c.name;

rows: Scans entire table heap sequentially from first to last page.
Small tables (<1000 rows) or queries returning >20% of the table.
Traverses B-tree to leaf, then fetches each row individually from heap.
Queries retrieving a small percentage of rows by an indexed filter.
Reads all required data directly from index leaf pages (zero heap reads).
Optimal for high-throughput queries with covering indexes.
Gathers matched row pointers into an in-memory bitmap, then reads heap pages sequentially.
Filtering by multiple conditions with `OR` or range queries.

data.text: Reading a Real Plan Line by Line

Read a plan from the inside out: the innermost nodes run first and feed their parents. For each node, compare `rows=` (the estimate) with `actual rows=` (the truth) and, in `BUFFERS` output, compare `shared hit` with `shared read`. A large gap between estimated and actual rows is the signal that statistics are stale. A high `shared read` on a node that runs many times is the signal that the working set does not fit in cache.

data.title: Spotting a misestimated join
data.content: The planner expected 10 rows from the filter but found 5000, so it chose a nested loop that then executed 5000 times. Fixing the statistics usually fixes the plan.
data.code:
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
SELECT c.name, o.amount
FROM customers AS c
JOIN orders    AS o
  ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.status = 'PENDING';

-- Nested Loop  (actual time=0.05..812.4 rows=5000 loops=1)
--   Buffers: shared hit=10234 read=612
--   ->  Seq Scan on orders o
--         Filter: (status = 'PENDING'::text)
--         Rows Removed by Filter: 995000
--         actual rows=5000 loops=1        <-- estimate expected 10
--   ->  Index Scan using customers_pkey on customers c
--         Index Cond: (id = o.customer_id)
--         actual rows=1 loops=5000

ANALYZE orders;   -- refresh stats, then re-run EXPLAIN

data.title: Interview angle: cost is a unit-less number, time is the truth
data.text: An interviewer will often show a plan and ask what is wrong. The first pass is costs and time: `EXPLAIN` alone gives estimates in arbitrary cost units, while `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` gives real milliseconds. The second pass is row estimates versus actual rows, because the planner's mistakes come from there. The third pass is buffers, to separate a slow query from a query that is simply reading a lot from disk. Being able to name those three passes in order is a much stronger answer than quoting a node name.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `EXPLAIN` estimates cost; `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` measures actual execution runtime.
Compare `rows=...` (estimated) with `actual rows=...` to detect stale statistics.
`BUFFERS` shows shared buffer cache hits vs physical disk reads.
